competencyModels.name: Data Science Professional Competency Model
competencyModels.description: Defines the core competencies required for data science roles, from junior analyst to senior data scientist, aligned to an Evidence Centred Design (ECD) assessment framework.

competencies.name: Statistical Reasoning
competencies.description: Ability to apply statistical concepts and methods to draw valid conclusions from data.

levels.label: Novice
levels.descriptor: Understands basic descriptive statistics (mean, median, variance).

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Applies hypothesis testing and confidence intervals correctly.

levels.label: Expert
levels.descriptor: Designs experiments and selects appropriate inferential methods for complex problems.

indicators: Correctly interprets p-values and confidence intervals
Selects appropriate statistical test for a given data type
Identifies violations of statistical assumptions

competencies.name: Programming & Data Manipulation
competencies.description: Proficiency in writing efficient code to clean, transform, and analyze data.

levels.label: Novice
levels.descriptor: Writes basic scripts to load and filter data.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Builds reusable data pipelines with error handling.

levels.label: Expert
levels.descriptor: Optimizes large-scale data processing workflows.

indicators: Writes clean, documented, version-controlled code
Uses vectorized operations for performance
Handles missing and malformed data robustly

competencies.name: Machine Learning Modeling
competencies.description: Ability to select, train, tune, and evaluate machine learning models appropriate to a business problem.

levels.label: Novice
levels.descriptor: Trains a single baseline model using default parameters.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Compares multiple algorithms and tunes hyperparameters systematically.

levels.label: Expert
levels.descriptor: Designs custom modeling approaches and diagnoses bias-variance tradeoffs.

indicators: Selects model class appropriate to problem and data
Applies cross-validation to avoid overfitting
Explains model performance using appropriate metrics

competencies.name: Data Visualization & Communication
competencies.description: Ability to translate analytical findings into clear visual and narrative form for varied audiences.

levels.label: Novice
levels.descriptor: Produces basic charts with correct labeling.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Designs dashboards tailored to stakeholder needs.

levels.label: Expert
levels.descriptor: Crafts compelling data narratives that drive decisions.

indicators: Chooses chart type appropriate to the data and message
Avoids misleading visual encodings
Tailors communication style to audience expertise

competencies.name: Ethical & Responsible AI Practice
competencies.description: Awareness of fairness, privacy, and governance considerations in data-driven work.

levels.label: Novice
levels.descriptor: Recognizes common sources of bias in data.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Applies fairness checks and documents data provenance.

levels.label: Expert
levels.descriptor: Leads governance reviews and mitigates systemic bias risks.

indicators: Identifies potential bias or privacy risk in a dataset
Applies relevant data protection principles
Documents model limitations and intended use

competencies.name: Business Problem Framing
competencies.description: Ability to translate an ambiguous business question into a well-defined analytical problem.

levels.label: Novice
levels.descriptor: Restates a business question in analytical terms with guidance.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Independently scopes an analysis plan aligned to business goals.

levels.label: Expert
levels.descriptor: Anticipates downstream business impact and reframes problems proactively.

indicators: Clarifies success metrics before starting analysis
Identifies relevant data sources for a business question
Aligns analytical scope with stakeholder priorities

competencyModels.name: People Leadership Competency Model
competencyModels.description: Core competencies for people managers responsible for leading teams, aligned to an ECD assessment framework for leadership development programs.

competencies.name: Strategic Thinking
competencies.description: Ability to align team goals with broader organizational strategy and anticipate future needs.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Understands team goals in relation to department objectives.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Connects team priorities to organizational strategy.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Shapes strategy and anticipates market or organizational shifts.

indicators: Articulates how team work supports company goals
Anticipates risks and opportunities in planning
Balances short-term delivery with long-term direction

competencies.name: Coaching & Development
competencies.description: Ability to support the growth of individual team members through feedback and development planning.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Gives basic performance feedback when prompted.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Proactively coaches team members using structured feedback models.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Builds development plans that grow future leaders.

indicators: Delivers specific, actionable feedback
Creates individualized growth plans
Recognizes and nurtures team member strengths

competencies.name: Decision Making
competencies.description: Ability to make timely, well-reasoned decisions under uncertainty.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Makes routine decisions with clear guidelines.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Weighs tradeoffs and makes sound decisions with incomplete information.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Makes high-stakes decisions and owns outcomes transparently.

indicators: Gathers relevant input before deciding
Considers multiple options and their tradeoffs
Takes ownership and adjusts course when needed

competencies.name: Communication & Influence
competencies.description: Ability to communicate clearly and influence outcomes without formal authority.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Communicates clearly within the immediate team.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Adapts communication style across stakeholders.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Influences senior stakeholders and drives organizational alignment.

indicators: Tailors message to audience and context
Builds consensus across differing viewpoints
Communicates difficult messages with clarity and empathy

competencies.name: Team Building & Collaboration
competencies.description: Ability to build a cohesive, high-performing team culture.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Participates constructively in team activities.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Fosters collaboration and resolves interpersonal conflicts.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Builds a strong team culture that scales across the organization.

indicators: Facilitates effective team collaboration
Resolves conflict constructively
Promotes psychological safety within the team

competencies.name: Accountability & Execution
competencies.description: Ability to drive results and hold self and others accountable for commitments.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Meets individual commitments consistently.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Holds team accountable to shared goals and deadlines.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Establishes accountability systems that scale across teams.

indicators: Sets clear expectations and deadlines
Follows through on commitments
Addresses underperformance directly and fairly
